threads.body: [Testing] The new payload-encoding path has no coverage: the integration test asserts only the request and dispatch spans. Add an operation that triggers encoding and assert the `request_encoding` span and its parent so this advertised behavior cannot regress unnoticed.
[Style] `Span.setAttribute` already ignores null values, so this conditional is redundant and creates an unnecessary special path.
Newer version doesn't generate encoding and dispatch spans? I think we could consider skipping these.

threads.body: `clientContext` accepts an arbitrary `Map<String, Object>` and does not reject null values, so a null entry makes this `toString()` throw before `span.end()` runs. Ignore null values (as the OpenTelemetry attribute API does) so user-provided diagnostic context cannot break request completion or leave the span unfinished.

replies.body:
Addressed in 45e7f747b36c2994678d82cad2bdb3ab0e0c16e8.

Analysis: The client context map can contain null values. Calling `toString()` on one throws before the request span ends. The test now includes a null value and uses exact assertions to prove that the adapter ignores it without adding an attribute.

Upsides: Request completion cannot fail on a null diagnostic value. Exact assertions also catch extra adapter attributes.

Downsides: Null client context entries are dropped instead of being represented in telemetry.

threads.body: [Style] This null guard is redundant: every branch ultimately calls `Span.setAttribute`, which already ignores a null value. Passing it through keeps this translation path simpler.

replies.body:
Addressed in daacd9bb43b410954765f2e6099dae44d037f0ed.

Analysis: OpenTelemetry `Span.setAttribute` ignores null string values. Each path in this method either calls that API or does nothing because the attribute is not enabled, so the early return adds no behavior.

Upsides: The translation method relies on the attribute API's documented null handling and has one less branch.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [General] Couchbase 3.0 can retry a request after a channel closes without calling `stopDispatch()` for the abandoned attempt; the next `startDispatch()` then overwrites this field, leaving the previous child span permanently unfinished. Terminal failures can likewise finish the request while a dispatch span is still active. End and clear active child spans both before replacing them and when the request finishes, and cover the retry/failure path in a test.

replies.body:
Addressed in 91da4eccade73d60b33c99d670f1aad97c00e56e.

Analysis: Couchbase 3.0's `KeyValueMessageHandler.channelInactive()` retries each in-flight request without calling `stopDispatch()`. A later dispatch replaces the stored span, and a terminal request finish can leave the last child active. The adapter now ends and clears encoding and dispatch spans before replacement and before the request span ends. The test exercises repeated starts followed by a finish with no matching stops.

Upsides: Retries and terminal failures no longer leak child spans. Clearing references also prevents a later stop from ending an old span twice.

Downsides: An abandoned dispatch span ends without `peer.latency` because Couchbase has not received a server response.
